title: An AI-assisted Android life sim: checking onboarding and saved progress
author: 1Life_Architect
selftext:
I'm the creator of Kommersant: City and Business, an offline Android life-and-business sim. AI tools helped with implementation and illustrations. I used them iteratively while checking the actual game screens and keeping a separate record of what was tested.



For the current 0.7.4 release, the QA checklist follows a clean first launch through all four tutorial steps. It also checks that question overlays leave the answers readable, free rest works in a controlled zero-energy test state, and the tested update preserved the checked saved fields, including money and progress. The signed build was exercised in an isolated Android API 36 emulator; those results don't establish coverage on every phone, and I haven't yet personally verified a fresh Google Play download on a physical device.



One useful habit has been keeping experimental content separate from the exact build being released. The store screenshots and posts show the tested free version; ideas for the next update stay out of its feature claims.



The game combines work shifts with decisions about money and three small business projects. It's public, free, and has no ads or real-money purchases. Saves stay on the device.



[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kommersant.prototype](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kommersant.prototype)



For other AI-assisted game developers: how do you record saved-progress migration checks so a later generated change doesn't silently invalidate the earlier results?
